5. He was implicated in Kayra PS Case No. 1 (2)/83 being Sessions Case No. 190 of 1986 (Gang Case) under section 400 of the Penal Code and also implicated in another Special Tribunal Case No. 128 of 1984 being Satkhira PS case No. 3 dated 18.1.84 under the Arms Act. In Sessions Case No. 103 of 1981 he was acquitted on 13.11.83. About these three cases we will deal with later on separately. 

 6. In the affidavit of the State it is stated that the detenu Md. Nazrul Islam was arrested on 30.11.80 in connection with Kayra PS Case No. 1 dated 18.11.80 under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code which was tried by the Sessions Judge, Khulna, in Sessions Case No. 103 of 1981 and the detenu was acquitted on 13.11.83. He was also implicated in Satkhira PS Case No. 22 dated 19.06.80 under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and that case ended in FRT on 11.12.83 which was accepted by the Magistrate on the same day, but the discharge certificate was sent to the detenu on 25.10.92 i.e. after issuance of the Rule by this Court. He was also implicated in Kayra PS Case No.9 dated 26.07.78 under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code which ended in FRT on 17.10.79 and he was discharged from the case on 12.12.79, but this order of discharge was not communicated to the jail authority till before 25.10.92. It is further stated that at present there is no case against him pending in the district of Satkhira. This detenu Md. Nazrul Islam was also made an accused in Mongla PS Case No.4 dated 10.03.80 under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and in that case after investigation FRT was submitted on 27.09.80 which was accepted by the Magistrate on 22.10.80, but there was further investigation into the case by the CID which also submitted final report on 10.06.83 and the same was accepted by the Magistrate on 08.09.83, but no discharged certificate was sent to the detenu in jail. This detenu was shown an accused in Mongla PS Case No. 10 dated 22.05.80 under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and after investigation police submitted FRT on 13.07.81 which was accepted by the Magistrate on 20.07.81, but there was further investigation into the case by CID which also submitted a final report on 02.08.83, but no discharge certificate was issued to the detenu from the Court of the Magistrate. 

 10. In Kayra PS Case No.1 dated 18.11.80 (Sessions Case No. 103 of 1981) the detenu was made an accused, but he was ultimately acquitted on trial by the Sessions Judge, Khulna. In Kayra PS Case No. 1(2) of 1983 (Sessions Case. No. 190 of 1986) (Gang Case) the detenu was made an accused He was tried along with other adult accused and found guilty under section 400 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and also to pay a fine of Tk. 1000/0, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more. This sentence expired on 15.03.92. The trial was held in the court of the Sessions Judge, Khulna, in Satkhira PS case No. 3 which is an arms case in which he was acquitted on 30.06.92. It is alleged that while he was in custody in the year 1984, he made a confession to the effect that he kept arms in his house. The police took the detenu to his house and allegedly recovered the arms from his house and this case under the Arms Act was started in the year 1984 after four years from the date of his arrest. Now, in these three cases it appears that the detenu was tried and in two cases he was acquitted and in another Gang Case he was convicted. 

 11. The learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State submits that he has nothing more to submit excepting the statements made in the affidavit from the State which was sworn by the Deputy Commissioner, Satkhira. Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq, the learned Amicus Curiae, has advanced much submissions on those three cases. As regards other cases Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq submits that in fact there was no case against the detenu and in spite of that he was being detained most illegally and without jurisdiction and every moment of his detention should be declared illegal and void. As regards these three cases which were tried by the Courts Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq submits that the proceedings of these three cases in respect of the present detenu are also void ab initio. In this connection Mr. Rafuq-ul-Huq has drawn our attention to the different sections of the Children Act, 1974 which was modified upto 31st of May, 1983. This Children Act of 1974 came into effect only for Dhaka District vide notification dated 11.09.76 and for all other districts it came into effect from 1st of June, 1980. Mr Huq has referred to various sections of the Children Act, particularly, sections 2(f), 6, 8, 15,48,49, 50, 51, 53, 54, 66 and 71. Section 2(f) provides that a boy under the age of 16 is called a child. Section 6 speaks that-no joint trial of the child and adult can be held. No child is to be charged with, or tried for, any offence together with an adult Even if the offence may be same of the child and adult, that must be tried separately. The child must be tried in the Juvenile Court and not in ordinary Court. Section 8 speaks that only the adult can be committed to court of Sessions and the Juvenile Court will take cognizance of the juvenile offenders. Section 15 shows the factors to be taken into consideration for passing orders by the Court with regard to juvenile offenders. The character and the age of the child and the circumstances in which the child is living are to be considered. Sections 48 and 49 provide that when a child is arrested in a non-bailable offence and cannot be brought forthwith before the Court, the Officer-in-Charge of the police station may release him on bail and if bail cannot be granted, the officer-in-charge of the police station shall keep him detained in a remand home or place of safety until he can be brought before the Court. If bail cannot be granted, the court shall send him to remand home or a place of safety. Sections 50-54 provide as to how the juvenile offenders are to be treated and tried in different manners by the Court. Section 41 shows that even the words 'conviction' and 'sentence' cannot be used in relation to children. So, the provisions of this Children Act have provided different processes and modes of arrest, detention and trial of the juvenile offenders under the age of 16 years in Children Act Mr. Huq submits that in the aforesaid three criminal cases no provisions of this Children Act were ever followed by the Courts and as such the trial in the aforesaid three cases are absolutely void and without jurisdiction. From the record, as far as available, it appears that in Sessions Case No. 103 of 1981 this minor boy was tried along with the adults by the Sessions Judge, Khulna, in which he was acquitted on 13.11.83. In the aforesaid Gang Case, namely, sessions Case No. 190 of 1986 he was tried and convicted under section 400 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years with fine. In this case he was tried and convicted along with all the adult dacoits.
